items.q: Ali has 12 stickers. Mei has 8 stickers. How many more stickers does Ali have than Mei?
items.hint: The extra part of the long strip is the gap. Take the small number from the big number.
steps: Ali's strip is longer.
The gap is 12 take away 8.
Ali has 4 more stickers.

items.q: Mei has 9 stickers. Ali has 5 stickers. Which sentence finds how many more stickers Mei has than Ali?
items.hint: Mei's strip is longer. The gap is the long strip take away the short strip.
steps: Mei has more, so her strip is longer.
How many more is the gap: the long strip take away the short strip.
9 - 5 finds the gap.

slips.say: 9 + 5 joins the strips. How many more asks for the gap.

items.q: Siti has 10 beads. Dev has 4 more beads than Siti. How many beads do they have altogether?
items.hint: Find Dev's beads first. Then join the two strips.
steps: Dev has Siti's 10 beads and 4 more: 14.
Join the strips: 10 + 14.
They have 24 beads altogether.

slips.say: 14 is only Dev's beads. Altogether means both strips joined.
4 is how many more Dev has. Altogether is the whole line of strips.

tpl.q: Siti has {a} beads. Dev has {d} more beads than Siti. How many beads do they have altogether?
tpl.hint: Find Dev's beads first. Then join the two strips.
steps: Dev has Siti's {a} beads and {d} more.
Join the strips: Siti's {a} and Dev's beads.
They have {ans} beads altogether.

items.q: Ali and Mei have 40 stickers altogether. Ali has 8 more stickers than Mei. How many stickers does Mei have?
items.hint: Take the extra part away from the total. Share what is left between two equal strips.
steps: Take away Ali's extra 8: 40 take away 8 is 32.
Two equal strips share 32: 16 each.
Mei has 16 stickers.

slips.say: 20 is half of 40, but Ali has more than Mei. Take away the extra part first.
24 is Ali's stickers. The question asks for Mei.

tpl.q: Ali and Mei have {T} stickers altogether. Ali has {d} more stickers than Mei. How many stickers does Mei have?
tpl.hint: Take the extra part away from the total. Share what is left between two equal strips.
steps: Take away Ali's extra {d} from {T}.
Two equal strips share what is left.
Mei has {ans} stickers.

items.q: Ali has 30 stickers. Mei has 18 stickers. Ali gives some stickers to Mei so they have the same number. How many stickers does Ali give?
items.hint: Find the gap. Ali gives half of the gap.
steps: The gap is 30 take away 18, which is 12.
Ali gives half of the gap: 6.
Then both have 24.

slips.say: 12 is the whole gap. If Ali gave 12, Mei would have more than Ali.

tpl.q: Ali has {a} stickers. Mei has {b} stickers. Ali gives some stickers to Mei so they have the same number. How many stickers does Ali give?
tpl.hint: Find the gap. Ali gives half of the gap.
steps: The gap is {a} take away {b}.
Ali gives half of the gap.
Ali gives {ans} stickers.

items.q: Wei has 18 fewer marbles than Ravi. Ravi has 52 marbles. How many marbles does Wei have?
items.hint: Ravi has more. Wei's strip is Ravi's strip with the fewer part taken off.
steps: Ravi has more, so his strip is longer.
Wei has 18 fewer: 52 take away 18.
Wei has 34 marbles.

slips.say: 70 adds. Wei has fewer than Ravi, so take away.

tpl.q: Wei has {d} fewer marbles than Ravi. Ravi has {r} marbles. How many marbles does Wei have?
tpl.hint: Ravi has more. Wei's strip is Ravi's strip with the fewer part taken off.
steps: Ravi has more, so his strip is longer.
Wei has {d} fewer: {r} take away {d}.
Wei has {ans} marbles.

items.q: 52 books are on two shelves. 7 books move from the top shelf to the bottom shelf. Then both shelves have the same number. How many books were on the top shelf at first?
items.hint: Share the total between two equal strips. Then put the moved books back.
steps: 52 shared into two equal strips is 26 each.
The top shelf gave away 7 to get to 26.
At first the top shelf had 26 + 7 = 33.

slips.say: 26 is each shelf after the move. The top shelf gave away 7 first.
19 is the bottom shelf at first. The question asks for the top shelf.

tpl.q: {T} books are on two shelves. {m} books move from the top shelf to the bottom shelf. Then both shelves have the same number. How many books were on the top shelf at first?
tpl.hint: Share the total between two equal strips. Then put the moved books back.
steps: {T} shared into two equal strips is half of {T} each.
The top shelf gave away {m} to get there.
At first the top shelf had {ans} books.

items.q: Ali, Ben and Mei have 90 cards altogether. Ben has 10 more cards than Ali. Mei has 10 more cards than Ben. How many cards does Ali have?
items.hint: Take away the extra parts. What is left is three equal strips.
steps: Ben has 10 more than Ali. Mei has 20 more than Ali.
Take away the extra 10 and 20: 90 take away 30 is 60.
Three equal strips share 60: Ali has 20.

slips.say: 30 is 90 shared into three equal strips, but the strips are not equal. Take away the extra parts first.

tpl.q: Ali, Ben and Mei have {T} cards altogether. Ben has {d} more cards than Ali. Mei has {d} more cards than Ben. How many cards does Ali have?
tpl.hint: Take away the extra parts. What is left is three equal strips.
steps: Take away the extra parts from the total.
Three equal strips share what is left.
Ali has {ans} cards.

items.q: Make up your own strip puzzle for a grown-up. Give the total and how many more, and ask for each child's number.
items.hint: Pick the two numbers first. Then work out the total and the gap.
steps: Check your puzzle with strips or boxes.
Make sure the total is even when one child has some more than the other.
Ask a grown-up to solve it without looking at your numbers.
